Yep: setting the `display` field of the `Style` component to `Display::None` will cause the text to not be rendered, but will affect layout in undesirable ways.

As will setting the text to an empty string.

Setting the color of the text to be fully transparent might work, but that's a bit of a hack.

It seems the recommended way to do it in html is by changing the opacity, which is in the color in Bevy
https://html-online.com/articles/blinking-text-css-animation/
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16344354/how-to-make-blinking-flashing-text-with-css-3

As Bevy UI is following flex box conventions, it would be the right way to do it

> As Bevy UI is following flex box conventions, it would be the right way to do it

I don't particularly like this answer, but under the current paradigm you're completely correct. I'll close this out then, and we can discuss "should we be following the flex box convention" elsewhere.

> 
> As Bevy UI is following flex box conventions, it would be the right way to do it

I think these examples use the transparency in order to get a fade-in fade-out animation. There is a [`visibility` property in CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/visibility) which definition is: "The visibility CSS property shows or hides an element without changing the layout of a document."

Also, if we choose transparency as the recommended solution, we should optimize it by skipping rendering in that case.

> I think these examples use the transparency in order to get a fade-in fade-out animation

Ha you're right, the first few results of googling "how to do blinking text in html" seems to do it with an animation
Reopening due to the mentioned 'visibility' property.
Yeah I think it makes sense to re-add Visibility

issue.body:
# Objective

Fixes #3422 

## Solution

Adds the existing `Visibility` component to UI bundles and checks for it in the extract phase of the render app.

The `ComputedVisibility` component was not added. I don't think the UI camera needs frustum culling, but having `RenderLayers` work may be desirable. However I think we would need to change `check_visibility()` to differentiate between 2d, 3d and UI entities.
